articles.title: El Burgos ata a David González... ¡hasta 2031!
articles.standfirst: El centrocampista, apodado el 'Ilusionista', amplía su contrato cuatro temporadas más
articles.summary: El centrocampista, apodado el 'Ilusionista', amplía su contrato cuatro temporadas más
articles.body: El Burgos se asegura talento para rato. David González seguirá vistiendo de blanquinegro hasta 2031, después de ampliar su contrato por cuatro temporadas más, además de la actual. El club burgalés blinda así a uno de sus futbolistas más destacados y apuesta por la continuidad de un jugador que representa como pocos la conexión entre el equipo y la ciudad. A sus 24 años, el centrocampista, que precisamente se retiró lesionado en el partido ante el Sabadell, se ha consolidado como una de las piezas importantes del conjunto de El Plantío. Sus números desde que regresó en 2024 hablan por sí solos: 86 partidos oficiales, 19 goles y nueve asistencias. Un rendimiento que confirma su capacidad para marcar diferencias y que ha reforzado su peso dentro del proyecto deportivo. El apodo de 'Ilusionista', utilizado por el propio club en el anuncio de la renovación, encaja con la apuesta por un jugador con talento ofensivo y capacidad para aportar en los metros decisivos. La historia de David con el Burgos viene de lejos. El centrocampista pasó siete temporadas en la cantera blanquinegra antes de continuar su formación en el Numancia y dar el salto a la estructura del Real Madrid. En 2024 regresó a casa para iniciar una nueva etapa en el fútbol profesional. Ahora, con su renovación hasta 2031, el Burgos refuerza su apuesta por un jugador de la tierra que ha convertido su regreso en una historia de crecimiento y compromiso.

articles.title: Jota: Celtic winger insists he is stronger after wrestling 'demons' during 18-month injury absence
articles.summary: The Portuguese winger was out for 18 months with a knee injury; he made his Celtic Park return off the bench in Sunday's 7-1 win against Hearts; watch Hibernian vs Celtic on Sunday from 11am, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
The Portuguese player took another major step in his comeback when he returned to Celtic Park action as a half-time substitute in Sunday's 7-1 demolition of Hearts .

The 27-year-old suffered a serious knee injury as Celtic clinched the title at Tannadice in April 2025, just as he was rediscovering his form after a difficult time in between spells at Parkhead.

He had joined Saudi club Al Ittihad and soon found himself unable to play when the club went over their foreign players quota, before a frustrating stint at Rennes.

The recovery from injury was far from smooth, but he is determined to make the most of his fitness.

"In the end, it's part of everyone's life," he said. "Everyone struggles, but certainly other people have worse problems.

"So I'm just grateful and privileged to be in such a wonderful sport and to have all of these experiences.

"I've met some demons and I've had some good talks with them. I think we developed a good relationship and we are all on the same table nowadays and we can laugh about everything that happened.

"If you don't grow from a situation like this, it's because you didn't learn anything.

"I could step away, see different things from other perspectives and value some stuff that maybe I wasn't valuing before.

"And now it's good because I have a clear idea of what I want, what I am. I might have it before as well, but now it's a bit clearer.

"The happiest thing in life for me is to play football. I couldn't in the last year or so. So right now, every time I step on a training pitch or a football pitch, for me it's everything. That's why I'm enjoying so much and valuing this so much."

The former Benfica player, who is not in Celtic's Europa League squad, revealed his "passion for football" was his motivation.

"My love for football is immense," he added. "Maybe someone else wouldn't want to come back because of the struggle or some guys just don't have that in themselves. That was my fuel to keep on working every day, to be healthy and fit, even if things weren't going that way.

"This is my dream. It's my passion. So there's moments where you reflect, there's moments where you're down and you cannot see any light, but that doesn't mean that you stop believing. You just need to find another way.

"But in the end, my aim was always to come back fit, whatever time I need to take, because I still have a long career in front of me and I'm still young.

"So there's no rush, let's do everything correctly and just trust the process."

When asked if he felt he was making up for lost time, Jota said: "There's no lost time because I grew a lot. It had to be what it had to be and I didn't lose. I actually gained because I'm way stronger nowadays."

articles.title: Caso Güler: "Como no hay evidencia, no se puede intervenir", dice el CTA
articles.standfirst: Ninguna de las 23 cámaras dispuestas en el Bernabéu tuvieron el "suficiente detalle" para arrojar "pruebas concluyentes"
articles.summary: Ninguna de las 23 cámaras dispuestas en el Bernabéu tuvieron el "suficiente detalle" para arrojar "pruebas concluyentes"
articles.body: La polémica desatada a raíz del codazo de Arda Güler a Peque durante la primera parte del Real Madrid-Sevilla con el resultado de 0-0, que ha indignado al sevillismo que considera que el turco debería haber sido expulsado, ha señalado directamente a la sala VAR y a la realización televisiva, producida desde la temporada pasada por Global Futbol Production (GFP). Fuentes de LaLiga, contactadas por este periódico, han explicado que la razón por la que no hay una toma clara de la jugada a pesar de que se utilizaron 23 para la retransmisión del partido se debe a que sólo las de tiro más amplio -la del fondo, la Skycam y la prevista para los fueras de jeugo- captaron la imagen. No fue un error de realización, simplemente que no existe. Y la señal que llega al camión de televisión que emite las imágenes en todos los hogares, aseguran, es la misma que el equipo de Cuadra Fernández, el responsable del VAR en el partido del Bernabéu. Mientras, otras fuentes del Comité Técnico de Árbitros (CTA) apuntaron a que "de las múltiples cámaras que hay en el partido, no todas valen para el VAR. La acción ocurre a espaldas del árbitro, zona fuera de balón. Las cámaras no estaban enfocando ahí, sólo las que tienen un tiro muy abierto. Como se ha visto, la acción aparece, pero no hay detalle". Y añaden que "no se aprecia si le da con el hombro, con el codo, con la mano, en la cara... No se ve. Y como no hay evidencia, no se puede intervenir. En el campo no se sancionó y el VAR, sin pruebas concluyentes, no puede hacer nada". GFP recogió el testigo de Mediapro el año pasado. Es una sociedad conjunta formada por HBS (en la parte de producción) y la empresa tecnológica italiana NVP (en la parte de servicios técnicos). Firmó cinco temporadas con LaLiga, hasta la 29/30.

articles.title: Michigan HC Coy on Bryce Underwood-Tommy Carr QB1 Decision Ahead of Game vs. Cignetti, No. 6 Indiana
articles.summary: Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham is keeping his quarterback decision to himself ahead of Saturday's showdown against No. 6 Indiana.
articles.body:
Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham is keeping his quarterback decision to himself ahead of Saturday's showdown against No. 6 Indiana.

Per Larry Lage of the Associated Press, Whittingham said he has already decided whether Bryce Underwood or Tommy Carr will be the Wolverines' starting quarterback against the Hoosiers, but he doesn't want their opponents to know just yet.

"We're not going to tip our hand," Whittingham said Monday.

Underwood was benched at halftime against Penn State this past Saturday in favor of Carr, and the freshman led two touchdown drives in the third quarter and ran for a 12-yard touchdown late in the fourth quarter that gave Michigan the two-score lead it needed to hold on to a 21-18 win.

Underwood has failed to impress this season, throwing two interceptions against the Nittany Lions to bring his season total to six with just five touchdown passes. Meanwhile, Carr has the momentum of Saturday's win and the famed lineage as the grandson of Lloyd Carr, who coached the Wolverines to the 1997 national title, and Tom Curtis, who was an All-American defensive back and holds Michigan's career interceptions record.

Perhaps now is the right time for Whittingham to turn to Carr as the Wolverines (4-2) try to salvage their season with the Hoosiers (6-1) coming to town.

articles.title: El fútbol más cruel: el Tavernes destituye a su técnico una semana antes de jugar contra el Valencia
articles.standfirst: Carlos Sapiña había logrado el milagro de meter al equipo del grupo Sur de la Lliga Comunitat en la fase definitiva de la Copa y se iba a sentar en el banquillo de Mestalla
articles.summary: Carlos Sapiña había logrado el milagro de meter al equipo del grupo Sur de la Lliga Comunitat en la fase definitiva de la Copa y se iba a sentar en el banquillo de Mestalla
articles.body: Hay días que el fútbol es cruel. Y hoy es uno de ellos. La directiva del Tavernes, equipo del grupo Sur de la Lliga Comunitat ha decidido destituir a su entrenador, Carlos Sapiña, a falta de nueve días del partido más importante de la historia del club de La Safor. Sapiña había sido el artífice de uno de esos milagros que nos deja la competición del Ko y había llevado al equipo al sorteo de la Copa del Rey en la que aparecían ya los equipos de primera división. Los bombos le otorgaron el premio de jugar contra el Valencia y además se decidió que el partido se disputaría en Mestalla debido a las carencias del estadio del Tavernes em cuanto a aforo e iluminación. La decisión está tomada en base a los resultados ligueros. El equipo se dejó todo en la clasificación de la copa y en Liga suma solo tres de los 21 puntos que se han puesto en juego. Una victoria y seis derrotas se han llevado al técnico que el día 28 de octubre se iba a sentar en el banquillo de Mestalla para cumplir uno de sus grandes sueños con el resto de la plantilla. El Tavernes fue el campeón de la Nostra Copa y eso le permitió jugar el play off contra el UD Macarena al que superó en la tanda de penaltis llevándose la mayor alegría de su historia. Hay que recordar que este miércoles salen a la venta las entradas para el partido de Copa en Mestalla con precios que van de los 10 a los 15 euros y que el Tavernes pondrá autobuses gratuitos para sus aficionados.

articles.title: Premier League: Marc Guehi among six players not to take knee
articles.summary: Premier League clubs took the knee for the first time this season, but six players chose to remain standing.
articles.body:
Premier League clubs took the knee this weekend for the first time this season as part of October's No Room for Racism campaign.

But six players across five clubs chose to remain standing during the pre-match gesture:

Speaking before Manchester City 's Champions League game on Tuesday, Guehi was asked whether it had lost its impact.

"I haven't been taking the knee for a while now. I always clap, just because of what that actually signifies," said the England international.

"I don't think it's necessarily a football issue, I think it's a wider societal issue and football is just that beacon of hope to try and get the message out.

"The message is still there, which is great. More can always be done. I think we should see how we can move the campaign along."

The Premier League maintains that taking the knee is a decision led by the players and that it is supportive of whatever stance they choose to take.

Why are Premier League clubs still taking the knee?

Premier League players began taking the knee in 2020 following the death of George Floyd and the subsequent Black Lives Matter protests.

The campaign was limited to selected matches following an agreement by club captains before the 2022-23 campaign.

This season, captains agreed to take the knee during October's No Room For Racism fixtures, which coincide with Black History Month in the UK.

The other five players who did not take the knee this weekend have not publicly commented, but Leeds manager Daniel Farke explained Calvert-Lewin's position.

"Dom is more or less like, 'no, I don't go down. I show my respect by standing up'. Every individual is different and shows respect for this campaign in a different way," said Farke.

"It's definitely a good campaign and a good topic that football and sports, in general, support situations like this because a dressing room is a perfect example of how we should all live together."

"I feel kneeling has just become a part of the pre-match routine and at the moment it doesn't matter whether we kneel or stand, some of us still continue to receive abuse," he said at the time.

Announcing this month's campaign, , external the Premier League said: "Players will be taking the knee before kick-off during the next two match rounds to show unity against all forms of discrimination."

Kick It Out told BBC Sport that taking the knee "still has value in raising awareness of the structural inequalities that exist in football and society."

"We can also understand the reasons players might become frustrated with the pace of change," they added.

Between 2021-22 and 2025-26, reports of both discrimination and racism received by the charity more than doubled, and reached record levels last season.

High-profile cases have also highlighted the continuing abuse faced by players.

After England defender Jess Carter received racist abuse online during last summer's Women's Euros, the Lionesses stopped taking the knee.

"Taking the knee, that's not enough. We have done that for a while. The impact is not good enough, it's not as big as we think," said England manager Sarina Wiegman at the time.

In February, Burnley midfielder Hannibal Mejbri, Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana, Wolves striker Tolu Arokodare and Sunderland winger Romaine Mundle were all subjected to racist abuse on social media over a single weekend.

A BBC Sport investigation also identified 22,389 potentially abusive messages across Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and X over a separate weekend.

Nevertheless, 2025 YouGov polling , external found a majority of ethnic minority football fans in Britain still considered taking the knee important in tackling racism - although most football fans overall in England did not.

The No Room For Racism campaign extends beyond taking the knee.

"We are using the reach of our players to send an important message: we are united in the fight against racism," said Premier League chief executive Richard Masters.

Players have also helped develop educational resources about diversity, available to more than 19,000 primary schools across England and Wales.

"I think it's important for young people to see role models who look like them, to see that they can achieve anything. It doesn't matter who you are, what you do or how you look," said Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk as part of the campaign.

"It means a lot to me to represent my community on and off the pitch."

articles.title: Alineaciones probables del PSG - Barça de la tercera jornada de la Champions League
articles.standfirst: Flick tiene bajas importantes pero podrá apostar por un once competitivo
articles.summary: Flick tiene bajas importantes pero podrá apostar por un once competitivo
articles.body: El Barcelona visita París en el tercer encuentro de la fase de la liguilla de la Champions League. El conjunto catalán llega con bajas destacadas, pero podrá disponer de un once competitivo contra los de Luis Enrique. Hansi Flick no puede contar con Andreas Christensen, Roony Bardghji, Jules Koundé y Eric Garcia. Los cuatro por causa médica. El francés y el catalán se lesionaron en el cruce del pasado sábado contra el Betis. Pero Raphinha, que jugó unos minutos contra el conjunto andaluz tras superar sus molestias en el muslo que le forzaron a ser baja contra el Getafe y el Galatasaray, será titular en la punta de ataque. Luis Enrique, por su parte, no podrá disponer de Nuno Mendes, que sufrió una dolencia muscular este pasado fin de semana contra el Estrasburgo. Ambos equipos ganaron los dos primeros cruces de la Champions League y llegan al encuentro en un gran momento: el Barça ha vencido en los once encuentros que ha disputado y el PSG encadena seis victorias. En el torneo continental, el equipo galo lleva 12 encuentros invicto. Alineación probable del PSG: Safonov; Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Zaïre-Emery; Neves, Vitinha, Ruiz; Doué, Dembélé, Kvaratskhelia. articles.title: La Federación Portuguesa castiga a Cristiano por abandonar la selección
articles.standfirst: La sanción es la mínima: 30 días de suspensión y una multa económica de 255 euros
articles.summary: Con 30 días de suspensión y una multa económica de 255 euros
articles.body: El abandono de la selección de Cristiano Ronaldo ya tiene consecuencias... mínimas. La Federación de Fútbol de Portugal ha sancionado al jugador con 30 días de suspensión y una multa de 255 euros por marcharse de la concentración del combinado nacional en Dinamarca durante el último parón internacional. Sin embargo, como el día que Cristiano abandonó la selección fue el 30 de septiembre, con este castigo que le han impuesto podría disputar los próximos compromisos de Portugal, que se mide a Dinamarca, el 14 de noviembre, y a Gales, el 17. Según el Reglamento Disciplinario de la Federación Portuguesa de Fútbol (FPF), CR7 se arriesgaba a una sanción que podía incluir una suspensión de entre uno y seis meses y una multa económica. Al final, se ha quedado en lo mínimo: en 30 días. En la resolución del Consejo de Disciplina de la Federación Portuguesa de Fútbol (FPF) se lee lo siguiente: "En estos términos y con los fundamentos expuestos, el Consejo de Disciplina de la Federación Portuguesa de Fútbol decide, en el presente procedimiento, considerar plenamente justificada la acusación y, en consecuencia, condenar a Cristiano Ronaldo dos Santos Aveiro por la comisión, en una ocasión y de manera intencional, de la infracción disciplinaria prevista y sancionada por el párrafo 1 del artículo 160 de la RDFPF, aplicándole, en consecuencia, la sanción de suspensión por 30 (treinta) días y, adicionalmente, la sanción de una multa que se fija en 2,5 UC, es decir, 255,00 € (doscientos cincuenta y cinco euros)", se lee en la sentencia.

articles.title: España amplía su ventaja al frente del ranking FIFA
articles.standfirst: Estados Unidos y Alemania completan el podio mundial tras la última ventana internacional
articles.summary: Estados Unidos y Alemania completan el podio mundial tras la última ventana internacional
articles.body: España se mantiene como número 1 del ranking FIFA tras la actualización que tendrá lugar este martes. La selección que ahora dirige Sonia Bermúdez ha logrado ampliar su ventaja respecto a Estados Unidos -en 31.68 puntos- tras la victoria (0-2) y empate (2-2) firmados en suelo americano en la última ventana internacional. Alemania completa el podio, mientras que Inglaterra, Japón, Francia, Brasil, Suecia, Canadá y Dinamarca completan el top ten mundial. España suma 685 días al frente de la clasificación mundial, un primer puesto del que sólo han sido dueñas otras tres selecciones (Estados Unidos, Alemania, Suecia) desde que se instaurara en 2003. La vigente campeona del mundo y de la Nations League ascendió al primer puesto por primera vez en la actualización del 15 de diciembre de 2023 y permaneció en lo más alto de la tabla hasta que el 16 de agosto de 2024 descendió al tercer puesto. España regresó al primer puesto el 7 de agosto de 2025 y desde entonces no ha hecho más que ampliar su distancia respecto al resto de potencias. España aparecerá como primer cabeza de serie en los sorteos del Mundial de 2027 y de la Nations League de 2027, que se celebrarán después de la próxima ventana internacional donde la selección jugará otros dos amistosos internacionales -aún por oficializar-. El único movimiento del ranking entre las diez mejores potencias del mundo ha sido el ascenso de Dinamarca a la décima posición tras la victoria (3-4) y empate (1-1) ante Canadá en dos amistosos de la última ventana internacional. El combinado nórdico no estaba en una posición así desde el 13 de agosto de 2010, si bien su mejor clasificación histórica es el sexto puesto, cuya mejor clasificación es el sexto puesto que alcanzó en 2007 y 2009. El mayor ascenso (49 puestos) de la clasificación en esta actualización lo firma Malaui, que pasa del 153 al 104 tras sus victorias (2-0 y 0-7) ante Zimbabue en el torneo de clasificación olímpica en la confederación africana. En el envés de la moneda Egipto, el mayor descenso (14 puestos), que pasa del 99 al 113 tras no jugar en esta última ventana.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo Suspended, Fined for Leaving Portugal Training Camp Amid Jorge Jesus Rift Rumors
articles.summary: The Portugal Federation is suspending Cristiano Ronaldo for 30 days and fining him €255 ($285) after he left the national team's camp due to a dispute with coach Jorge Jesus during the most recent international window, per Fabrizio Romano.
articles.body:
The Portugal Federation is suspending Cristiano Ronaldo for 30 days and fining him €255 ($285) after he left the national team's camp due to a dispute with coach Jorge Jesus during the most recent international window, per Fabrizio Romano .

In a lengthy statement following his departure, Ronaldo did apologize for leaving the camp and said he would accept any punishments levied against him.

Ronaldo wasn't happy after being an unused substitute during a 2-1 win over Norway in UEFA Nations League action on Sept. 27. He said Jesus had told him to be ready to play 30 minutes in the match after initially believing he wouldn't be in the team's plans against Norway, and that the coach's public comments on the matter after the fact didn't match the conversation the two had privately.

Kobe's daughter features in in Victoria's Secret Fashion Show

But Ronaldo went on to acknowledge he handled the situation poorly.

"I owe my national team teammates an apology for leaving the training camp," he wrote. "Despite the absolute breach of trust in the coach's word, as anyone who witnessed our conversations can testify, I should not have done it. The responsibility is exclusively mine. I apologize to the Portuguese people, too, but a broken promise has, for me, a defining impact. I felt that from that moment on, my continued presence would only harm the group, and I did what I have always said I would do if I did not feel useful: I packed my bags and left. The consequence of my actions should be assessed and punished by the [FPF]. The punishment should not have any mitigating circumstances. I am not just any player; I am the captain of the team, and that constitutes an aggravating factor."

Ronaldo left the door open for continuing with the national team as well, a sentiment that is shared, with Portugal's Football Federation president Pedro Proença calling him "one of our key pieces."

It is fair to question at this point, however, if Portugal are better off on the pitch without the 41-year-old Ronaldo. While he did have three goals at this summer's World Cup, Portugal didn't advance past the Round of 16 and Ronaldo's limitations at this stage in his career—especially defensively—cannot be ignored.

But he's also a legend in his country and the optics of a hostile end to the relationship aren't great for either side. When Ronaldo does retire from international football, a celebration would be a more fitting conclusion.

articles.title: Ronaldo banned for 30 days, fined $285 by Portugal over spat with Jesus
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo handed month-long ban by the disciplinary council of Portugal’s Football Association.
articles.body:
Cristiano ‌Ronaldo has been suspended for 30 days by the ⁠Portuguese Football Association for leaving the national team camp following a rift with coach Jorge Jesus over ⁠his place in the side.

The federation’s disciplinary council said on Monday that it had upheld the charge against the 41-year-old ⁠forward in full and imposed a fine of 255 euros ($285).

Ronaldo left Portugal’s base in Copenhagen before their Nations League match against Denmark earlier this month, having accused Jesus of ‌twice breaking his word about his role after he was an unused substitute against Norway.

Jesus denied making any agreement with Ronaldo but left the door open for his return following Portugal’s 2-1 win.

The disciplinary council’s non-professional section found Ronaldo had intentionally committed an ⁠offence under Article 160(1) of the ⁠federation’s disciplinary regulations. Proceedings were opened on October 9 over facts reported two days earlier.

The statement did not specify which matches or activities ⁠the suspension would cover, or whether time already served under a provisional ⁠suspension would count towards the 30-day ⁠sanction.

Ronaldo later apologised for failing to acknowledge supporters after the Norway match and for leaving his teammates, saying he remained available for selection ‌after serving any punishment arising from the incident.

Portuguese FA President Pedro Proenca has said everyone within the federation ‌wanted ‌Ronaldo to return to the national team once the matter was resolved.

articles.title: Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage under increasing pressure after 5-0 defeat to Brighton
articles.summary: Former Lyon and Lens boss Pierre Sage was appointed Crystal Palace manager after Oliver Glasner left in the summer; the 47-year-old has won four of his 10 games in charge in all competitions; Palace lost 5-0 to rivals Brighton on Sunday
articles.body:
Palace find themselves 14th with seven points from seven games and Sage was unable to give assurances he had the club's full support after such a bitter defeat to their rivals.

Chairman Steve Parish recently stated the club was on "high alert" during the transitionary process from the era of Oliver Glasner into the new one under Sage, which includes a number of new players and a first Europa League campaign.

Asked after the defeat whether he would be given time to turn things around, Sage said: "I don't know.

"I just want to apologise to the fans because it's not normal to show this face for this club against this other club, and we are not at the level we expected.

"I am really sorry for that because I know how important it is for them.

"We didn't show that today it was really important for us too. We didn't understand in which context this game was played."

Sage has come under fire for his attacking approach at Palace, who have the worst defence in the Premier League after conceding 17 goals in seven matches.

Palace's defensive unit took a hit over the summer with the sales of Daniel Munoz and Maxence Lacroix, both of whom were big figures in the club's success under Glasner.

Palace signed central-defenders Axel Disasi and 18-year-old Honest Ahanor on loan in the summer to replace Lacroix and Marc Guehi, who left to join Manchester City in January of this year.

Anan Khalaili was brought in from Union Saint-Gilloise initially to compete with minutes for Munoz but his arrival ended up paving the way for the Colombian to leave.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo: Portugal captain punished over walkout following explosive row with head coach Jorge Jesus
articles.summary: Portugal captain Cristiano Ronaldo claimed head coach Jorge Jesus twice broke his word about the star's role in the team after he walked out on the national team's camp on the eve of a match; he has now been punished for his actions but will not miss any Portugal matches
articles.body:
The Portuguese FA's disciplinary council did not specify when Ronaldo's ban begins, but Sky Sports News understands it is enforced from the date he left the squad's training camp in Denmark on September 30.

It means the 41-year-old former Manchester United and Real Madrid star is available to play in Portugal's Nations League matches next month against Denmark and Wales if he is called upon by Jesus.

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner asked to be punished by the Portuguese FA when he posted a lengthy letter detailing the circumstances which led to his departure from the camp. Ronaldo said he wanted to be spared any leniency.

However, the player reported to be the highest-paid footballer in the world could pay off his fine from the Portuguese FA in 39 seconds based on his estimated wages at Saudi Pro League club Al Nassr.

Ronaldo reportedly earns £488,000 per day from his Al Nassr salary, while Forbes estimate his earnings for 2026 will reach £225m.

The captain's fall-out with Jesus began after he was an unused substitute in a 2-1 win over Norway in Oslo. Ronaldo claims he was told he would be brought on and had warmed up only for Jesus to change his mind.

Ronaldo missed the game against Denmark and the home match against Norway, both of which Portugal won to leave them top of Nations League Group A4 with a perfect record from four matches.

After the second win over Norway, Jesus insisted the door remained open for Ronaldo, who subsequently apologised for his actions and admitted he deserved to be sanctioned.

The Portuguese federation's disciplinary council announced Ronaldo's punishment in a 28-page document on Monday evening, saying it was "adequate and sufficient" for the player's "serious infraction".

Ronaldo is Portugal's record goalscorer and appearance holder with 146 goals in 234 caps. He said in his near-2000-word statement last month that he hopes his international career is not over yet.

Jesus did not comment when asked for his response to Ronaldo's lengthy statement to his 679 million Instagram followers. It is up to the Portugal head coach now to decide if Ronaldo is part of his plans for the next international break.

articles.title: UEFA writes letter to FIFA demanding answers over Gianni Infantino's presidency and his relationship with Donald Trump
articles.summary: FIFA has been given two weeks by UEFA to respond to the long list of concerns which were raised by European football leaders at the FIFA Council meeting in Zurich last Thursday, in the search for transparency over Gianni Infantino's dealings, including his relationship with Donald Trump
articles.body:
The letter, which has been seen by Sky Sports News , was written on Monday by UEFA secretary general Theodore Theodoridis and sent to his FIFA counterpart Mattias Grafstrom.

Sky Sports News has also obtained a copy of the full list of 42 questions which cover 12 topics, including 10 alleged conflicts of interest, across eight pages.

Theodoridis gives FIFA two weeks to respond to UEFA's long list of concerns which were raised by European football leaders at the FIFA Council meeting in Zurich last Thursday.

He begins by noting that Infantino acknowledged during the meeting that mistakes had been made but the explanations provided "have not begun satisfactorily to address a number of fundamental questions".

UEFA has also asked for an immediate audio recording of the meeting in another sign it is demanding full transparency from FIFA.

"These questions require answers now," Theodoridis writes. "They cannot be deferred until the next meeting of the FIFA Council - nor can future governance reforms substitute for scrutiny of decisions already taken and accountability for them."

The 42 questions are split into 12 sections:

1. FIFA Forward Enterprise - the World Cup sell-off proposal. Why did Infantino negotiate to sell off a stake in FIFA tournaments in secret?

"Could FIFA explain why an agreement granting exclusivity to Thrive Capital was signed without prior consultation of the FIFA Council? Who authorised FIFA to enter into this agreement, and on what basis?

"Why was the FIFA Council not consulted before exclusivity was granted, irrespective of any approval that may have been envisaged at a later stage?

"Could FIFA also confirm who the members of the Management Board Bureau were at the time of the decision and how each of them voted, specifying who voted in favour, who voted against and who abstained?

"When was it intended that the FFE proposal and supporting documentation would be submitted to the FIFA Council?"

2. Will investigation into FIFA governance be independent and why is FIFA blocking release of documents?

"How does FIFA intend to establish what actually happened in relation to FFE, the Balogun case and the other matters raised by members of the Council, and to ensure appropriate accountability for any shortcomings identified?"

3. Review of funding of FIFA's member associations. On what basis did FIFA propose to sell off a stake in World Cups at a valuation of $20bn when this summer's tournament generated revenues of $15bn?

"Please explain the investment and exit assumptions underlying Thrive Capital's proposed participation".

4. Development funding and use of FIFA's financial resources. Why were member associations going to receive development funding to accept the sell-off proposal when FIFA already has $6bn cash reserves?

"The FIFA president has repeatedly stated that FIFA's money belongs to its MAs. Why, then, was substantially increased funding for MAs presented in connection with FFE and external investment, rather than being financed directly from FIFA's own resources?

"What exactly were MAs being asked to approve as part of the FFE proposal in order to access these additional funds? Following the withdrawal of FFE, FIFA has now proposed increasing funding to $25m per MA using its own reserves. Why was such an approach not considered before FFE was proposed?"

5. Remuneration and financial transparency. Why did Infantino receive a £1.3m payment in 2024 on top of his £4m FIFA salary?

"Recent media reports, referring to filings by FIFA's US World Cup organising entity (FWC2026 US), indicate that the FIFA president received substantial additional remuneration which was not disclosed in FIFA's annual report.

"Could FIFA clarify the nature, amount and basis of these payments, why they were not disclosed in FIFA's annual report, and whether they were reviewed and approved by the competent FIFA bodies?

"Could FIFA also confirm whether the additional remuneration was treated as taxable income and whether the corresponding income tax was paid?"

6. Review of disciplinary procedures and the Balogun case. Why was Balogun allowed to play when he was suspended?

"President Trump publicly acknowledged having called the FIFA president to request a review of the Balogun disciplinary case. What exactly did he ask him to do, and what was his response? Would the case have been reviewed in the absence of his intervention?

"Following that conversation, did the FIFA president or the FIFA secretary general communicate with anyone within FIFA, including members of the administration or the chair of the disciplinary committee, concerning the Balogun case? If so, could FIFA specify with whom, when and the nature of those communications?"

7. Compliance with the Laws of the Game. Why was there a 27-minute World Cup final half-time show?

"The half-time interval during the World Cup final lasted 27 minutes, without any prior request to the IFAB and consultation with the FIFA Council.

"Similarly, the introduction of mandatory so called hydration breaks at all World Cup matches, in deviation from the existing rule was not preceded, to our knowledge, by consultation or a request for authorisation from the IFAB."

8. Electoral integrity and independence of FIFA's judicial bodies. UEFA doubts about whether FIFA presidential election will be fair.

"The official electoral campaign period began on 30 April 2026, the date of the FIFA Congress in Vancouver. Which body, in addition to the FIFA Electoral Committee, is responsible for overseeing the electoral process, and what procedures and safeguards have been established to prevent the misuse of FIFA resources and ensure a fair and impartial presidential election?

"We have concerns regarding the independence and impartiality of the chair of the FIFA Electoral Committee, Mr Chiomento, given the committee's crucial role in overseeing the presidential election."

9. Presidential expenditure and financial oversight. Infantino's private jet provided by Qatar Airways.

"Numerous media reports in recent years have raised questions concerning the FIFA president's use of private aircraft and the costs of his accommodation, notably in Qatar and the United States.

"Could FIFA provide a detailed account of the relevant expenditure, including its amounts, purposes, authorisation procedures and compliance with FIFA's applicable financial and travel policies?"

10. World Cup hospitality and allocation of privileges.

"We request access to the complete list of guests seated in the VIP and VVIP sections during the World Cup final, including their names, positions and the reasons for their invitations.

"Could FIFA also explain the criteria and decision-making process governing the allocation of these places, particularly in circumstances where numerous guests were apparently given priority over presidents of MAs and secretaries general of confederations?"

"In the absence of any prior involvement of the FIFA Council, who decided to establish the FIFA Peace Prize, for what purpose, and who decided that the President of the United States should receive it?

"What role did the FIFA president personally play in the creation of the award and the selection of its recipient? Were any independent selection procedures or objective criteria established and applied? If so, could FIFA provide the relevant documentation?"

"A series of decisions, transactions and interventions involving the FIFA president, the President of the United States and individuals associated with him raise serious questions concerning potential conflicts of interest, transparency and institutional accountability."

The FIFA Peace Prize, which was not submitted to the FIFA Council for approval.

The reported seven-year, approximately $4m lease of office premises in Trump Tower, New York, involving Eric Trump, for premises reportedly unused for much of the year.

The proposed agreement with Thrive Capital, led by Mr Joshua Kushner, a member of the US president's family.

The US president's telephone call to the FIFA president requesting intervention in the Balogun disciplinary case.

Reported advanced discussions involving the US president and individuals associated with him concerning a FIFA cryptocurrency.

The World Cup sponsorship arrangement with Kalshi, a company reportedly advised and partly owned by Donald Trump Jr, including reports that Kalshi received extensive advertising exposure without providing financial consideration to FIFA.

The last-minute relocation of the World Cup draw, reportedly at significant additional cost to FIFA, to the JFK/Donald Trump Center in Washington, DC, instead of Las Vegas.

The involvement of the US president's daughter and grandson in the Club World Cup draw.

The announcement of a $75m investment in Palestine during the US president's Board of Peace meeting, apparently without prior information being provided to, or approval sought from, the FIFA Finance Committee or Council.

Public statements by White House representatives, including Andrew Giuliani and the US president himself, defending the FIFA president, supporting his continued presidency and criticising those questioning his leadership.

UEFA has so far failed to put forward a candidate before the November 18 deadline to challenge Infantino in next March's presidential election.

Arsene Wenger would be a popular choice to take on Infantino but FIFA's global football development chief has made no comment about a potential challenge.

articles.title: Crystal Palace: Manager Pierre Sage facing a fight to keep his job
articles.summary: Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage faces a fight to keep his job, but will be given more time.
articles.body:
While no-one doubted that following in Oliver Glasner's footsteps as Crystal Palace manager would be a difficult task, Pierre Sage now finds his position under close scrutiny.

A string of poor results - most recently Sunday's 5-0 drubbing by Brighton - makes this week a crucial one in determining his future.

Sage has won just two of his opening seven Premier League games in charge, while the 17 goals they have conceded is the most in the league.

But there is a degree of sympathy from some behind the scenes at Selhurst Park that the Frenchman has been dealt a difficult hand.

Injuries have not been kind, while the absence of Jean-Philippe Mateta and Ismaila Sarr - due to a mixture of fitness and personal issues, related to both players' desire to leave the club - has not helped the start of his reign.

Co-owner and chairman Steve Parish is not one to act on impulse. He resisted the temptation to act when Glasner publicly criticised the club's board for "abandoning" the team after the decision to sell Marc Guehi to Manchester City in January.

Glasner saw out his contract and added the Europa Conference League title to the FA Cup won the season before.

Not that Sage is out of the woods. With crucial games against Besiktas and Newcastle on the horizon, further poor results will leave Parish with a decision to make.

Some figures close to Palace believe the writing is already on the wall and, when the right replacement is in place, his short tenure will come to an end.

But, having failed to appoint first-choice target Andoni Iraola following Glasner's exit, Palace are well aware of the difficulties of the managerial market.

What is for sure is that the 47-year-old is facing a fight to keep his job.

Sage feels 'shame' at Palace thrashing with future in doubt

Sage may point to the disbanding of the squad that led Palace to their first ever major trophies, with the FA Cup in 2025 before last season's Europa Conference League triumph, as the reason for his tough start to life in south London.

Eberechi Eze, Michael Olise, Maxence Lacroix, Daniel Munoz and Guehi have all departed Selhurst Park since the summer of 2024.

The departure of highly influential sporting director Dougie Freedman in 2025 has also been keenly felt.

In addition to Sage, the position of Freedman's replacement Matt Hobbs is also under the spotlight.

But conceding 17 goals in seven Premier League matches points to a problem, at least in part, of Sage's own making.

The team's recent DNA is rooted in defensive stability. Predecessors Glasner and Roy Hodgson produced well-organised teams with a solid base for its attacking players.

Conceding close to 2.5 goals per game is so far removed from what the team's recent successes has been built upon that it has raised major concern from the club's powerbrokers.

Palace are currently on course to concede 92 goals this season. No club has conceded more since Sheffield United shipped 104 goals to finish bottom in 2024.

Personnel is contributing to those defensive deficiencies. Losing Guehi, Lacroix and Munoz in the space of six months represent significant losses.

From the three centre-backs that started in Sunday's 5-0 loss to Brighton , Jaydee Canvot is 20 years old and Honest Ahanor only 18.

Nevertheless, there is a clear sense from inside the club that Sage's system and approach has been a major contributing factor towards their troubles in defence.

There is a perception from sections of supporters that the club's summer defensive recruitment has not helped.

Takehiro Tomiyasu, Ben Chilwell and Oscar Mingueza arrived on free transfers, while Axel Disasi and Ahanor arrived on loan.

As mitigation, it is understood Palace have encountered major difficulty in complying with Uefa's financial rules, leaving them hampered in the transfer market.

Trying to stay within Uefa's guidelines was among the reasons why the club sold Munoz to Nottingham Forest for £22m.

But those financial difficulties do not make the situation Sage finds himself any less critical.

With a Europa League trip to Besiktas and home Premier League game against Newcastle on the horizon, Sage has an opportunity to change the mood music.

Two positive results and the Frenchman will hope he can mount a more consistent upward trend.

Two defeats, however, and Palace may well feel that enough is enough.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo suspension: Portugal issues weak punishment to CR7 for national team walkout
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo's walkout on the Portugal national team last international break created global headlines as he abruptly left camp, but the "punishment" le...
articles.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo 's walkout on the Portugal national team last international break created global headlines, after the Selecao captain abruptly left camp ahead of their Nations League match at Denmark.

Following Portugal's win over Norway in which Ronaldo was an unused substitute, the 41-year-old was unhappy with the coaching staff for making him warm up on the sideline and then not bringing him into the match. He was seen darting down the tunnel instead of celebrating with his teammates, beginning speculation that he was frustrated with proceedings.

Ronaldo then left national team camp the day before their next match, while speculation and reporting swirled regarding the reason for his exit. The Al Nassr star later clarified his position in a lengthy statement which included demands of the head coach and an apology for his actions.

In that statement, Ronaldo said he would accept a punishment from the national team, saying as captain he should be held to a higher standard. That punishment was levied by the Portugal federation, and it was a big nothing burger.

Portugal 'suspend' Cristiano Ronaldo in name only

The Portuguese federation issued a suspension to captain Cristiano Ronaldo for leaving national team camp, but in practice the punishment has little actual effect.

Ronaldo was issued a suspension for 30 days, plus a meager fine of €255 ($286). On his Al Nassr salary of €180 million per year over two years, it would take Ronaldo approximately 43 seconds to earn the money to pay his fine.

The suspension will not keep Ronaldo out of action at all, as it is retroactive to the end of the last international break on October 9.

With Portugal not playing another game until November 14, Ronaldo will be available for selection in that game, according to a report by Portuguese outlet A Bola .

If Ronaldo is indeed available for selection in Portugal's next international window, he will be on hand to meet Denmark and Wales in the country's final two group stage games in 2026/27 UEFA Nations League play.

articles.title: Enzo Maresca hints a Manchester City superstar could play against AEK Athens – but is it worth the risk?
articles.summary: Erling Haaland sustained an injury in the closing stages of the hard-fought 3-2 win that Manchester City picked up over Ipswich Town on Saturday. Haaland pic...
articles.body:
Erling Haaland sustained an injury in the closing stages of the hard-fought 3-2 win that Manchester City picked up over Ipswich Town on Saturday. Haaland picked up a lower leg injury when he fired a shot away in the closing stages of the match at the Etihad Stadium and hobbled down the tunnel as soon as the final whistle blew. Enzo Maresca told the media earlier today that Haaland could be available for Manchester City's UEFA Champions League match week three match against AEK Athens tomorrow night. However, you do wonder if playing Haaland is worth the risk.

Enzo Maresca hasn't given up hope that Manchester City will have Erling Haaland available against AEK Athens.

Enzo Maresca did provide an update on the injury status of his squad when he faced the media earlier today. Maresca revealed that Haaland is in contention to play against AEK Athens tomorrow night. Speaking on Haaland's fitness after the injury he sustained against Ipswich Town, Maresca said: " He (Erling Haaland) can be available. We'll see. We have a session now and we have some doubts after Sunday's game. "

" He was quite good yesterday. Better. So we'll see today ."

" Replacing Erling is always difficult. We have some different options and we'll see tomorrow. "

" It depends a little bit on the gameplan and also there is a chance he can be available tomorrow ."

You do wonder if playing Haaland tomorrow night is worth the risk considering what City has on the horizon.

Following their loss to PSG last week, Manchester City do need to pick up all three points against AEK Athens tomorrow night. They will not want to lose ground in the chase for a top eight finish in the UEFA Champions League league phase table. So Enzo Maresca's side must pick up all three points against AEK Athens at home. Based on this, you could see Erling Haaland start tomorrow night if he is fit enough to play.

The question for me is: Is starting Erling Haaland worth the risk? Manchester City's next two Premier League fixtures are against Aston Villa at Villa Park and then City face high-flying Brighton at the Etihad Stadium. Those two matches will be tough tests for Enzo Maresca's side. City will need Haaland fit and firing for both of those matches. AEK Athens will be no pushover at the Etihad, but the safe option may be to have Haaland on the bench tomorrow night in case of an emergency. City cannot afford to push Erling Haaland too hard given his importance to them.

Enzo Maresca hasn't given up hope that Erling Haaland can play tomorrow night against AEK Athens. It remains to be seen if Haaland is fit enough to play but he didn't train with his teammates in Manchester City's open training session earlier today. So perhaps Haaland won't be ready to start tomorrow night but you do feel that starting Haaland isn't a risk worth taking given the challenges that City have on the horizon.

articles.summary: Utah-Houston is college football’s most expensive ticket this week as ESPN's "College GameDay" returns to Utah for a second straight weekend.
articles.body:
After bringing its traveling set to BYU last weekend, ESPN's "College GameDay" is staying in Utah for another week, moving roughly 45 miles north for what's turning out to be the priciest ticket in college football this weekend.

With the popular pregame show making back-to-back stops in the Beehive State, Utahns are getting hyped as the No. 10 Utes take on No. 14 Houston at Rice-Eccles Stadium with a get-in-price of $254 on TicketData.com , making it the most expensive matchup involving teams in the latest AP Top 25 poll. The price has increased 12% over the previous three days, and will most likely fluctuate as kickoff approaches.

Kickoff's set for 8:15 p.m. MDT this Saturday on ESPN. Weather-wise, fans can expect mostly clear skies in Salt Lake City with just a slight chance of light rain and temps hovering in the mid-40s.

The game will give the Utes a national stage in front of a home crowd, with "GameDay" set to broadcast from campus ahead of Saturday night's matchup. The three-hour show begins at 7 a.m. MDT.

The Utah-Houston matchup has plenty of juice beyond the "GameDay" spotlight. The Utes enter the weekend unbeaten and ranked 12th nationally in total defense and ninth in total offense, according to ESPN, making them one of the more balanced teams in the country. Houston can put that balance to the test, though, with the Cougars ranking 10th in total offense and bringing a strong attack into Rice-Eccles Stadium.

Utah got a reminder over the weekend that it can't afford to take its foot off the gas. The Utes jumped out to a 13-0 halftime lead against Colorado before the Buffaloes stormed back with 17 unanswered points in the third quarter.

Utah ultimately pulled out the 27-24 win, thanks in part to Devon Dampier's three touchdown passes and a late defensive stop that helped seal the game. Against a Houston offense ranked among the nation's best, the Utes will need to put together a more consistent four quarters if they want to keep their winning streak going.

The game in Salt Lake City leads the Week 7 slate involving AP Top 25 teams. No. 7 Ole Miss' trip to No. 19 Texas ranks second, with the cheapest available ticket listed at $230 on the same website. That price had fallen 28% over the previous three days.

Other notable matchups include No. 11 Tennessee at South Carolina for $157, No. 18 LSU at Auburn starting at $149 and No. 6 Indiana at Michigan for $134.

Meanwhile, the No. 2 BYU Cougars' trip to UCF had a listed entry price of $60, despite the team coming off a major win over Notre Dame. That price had risen 30% over the previous three days.

The contrast is notable after BYU-Notre Dame was among the most expensive games in the country last Saturday at around $429 on Wednesday.

The "GameDay" broadcast from BYU featured an early-morning crowd, Cosmo entertaining fans and ESPN personalities leaning into the Cougars' campus culture. The atmosphere carried into Saturday night, when BYU upset then-No. 2 Notre Dame 28-24 at LaVell Edwards Stadium.

Now, the show is making the short trip north to the Utes' home, giving the state a second consecutive weekend in the national spotlight.

The two campuses offer different backdrops for the broadcast. BYU's gathering showcased the Cougars' traditions and the anticipation surrounding a top-two opponent, while Utah's show will be staged at President's Circle in the heart of campus.

For the Utes, the visit arrives during an important stretch of the season. Utah is unbeaten and facing a ranked conference opponent, creating an opportunity to strengthen its College Football Playoff résumé ahead of its Nov. 7 matchup against the rival Cougars.

With the cheapest tickets topping the AP Top 25 slate and "GameDay" staying in Utah for another weekend, Salt Lake City is set to take center stage in college football.

articles.title: After chaotic weekend, what do we know about college football 2026?
articles.summary: The current poll has five undefeated teams in the top 10. An argument can be made all five — No. 1 Miami, 2. BYU, 5. Texas Tech, 9. Utah, 10. UCLA — are over...
articles.body:
A fourth team has emerged as No. 1 in the college football polls this week, and we are just past the midway point in the season.

You know the saying … "if you have four you have none."

OK, that may be true of quarterbacks when a coach cannot decided between two. But you get the idea.

Is there really a No. 1 team in college football this season? And if not, is that all bad?

Because if you have chaos at the top during the regular season that should set up an unpredictable, entertaining, highly competitive 12-team playoff.

The current Coaches Poll has five undefeated teams in the top 10, including No. 1 Miami. An argument can be made that all five are over-ranked.

Especially when you consider those five teams — Miami, BYU (3), Texas Tech (5), Utah (9) and UCLA (10), have combined to play three teams ranked at the time of the game.

The same number that No. 13 Alabama has played. And, yes, Ole Miss has played four but, sorry, the Rebels are not getting credit any longer for beating Louisville on a walk-off field goal.

Each team among the unbeatens can justify its ranking, some stronger than others. Similarly, a case can be made for each being over ranked.

Of course, none of this matters. What matters is the College Football Playoff Committee's final ranking Dec. 6.

And what criteria matters most to the committee this year. Is it eye test? Strength of schedule? The cryptic game control? How about head-to-head? Some combination of those?

We will learn more in two weeks when its first ranking is unveiled.

Just ask Notre Dame and Miami how that can change.

Five teams in the top 25 are unbeaten after Week 7. Exactly one year ago, that number was 12. What does that say? Hard to say but I know this: If I were a gambling man and pressured into taking one of those five or the field …

In fact, I will argue of those five teams, only Miami is a true national contender with BYU a dark horse. As for Texas Tech, Utah and UCLA … all headed for first-round playoff exits, if they make the playoffs.

One-loss teams such as Ohio State (2), Georgia (4), Indiana (6), Ole Miss (7), Notre Dame (8) and Tennessee (11); and two-loss Alabama (13), would be favored over Texas Tech, Utah and UCLA on any neutral field.

A year ago this week, Miami was No. 2 and Indiana No. 7. The Hurricanes then needed help to make the playoff after being squeezed out of the ACC title game. The Hoosiers got better and better and had the top seed entering the playoffs.

Of course, both were there at the end, playing a dramatic title game won by Indiana.

Miami is No. 1, but are the Hurricanes the best team in the country?

This unpredictable season was captured in one weekend that could have had any one of six teams come out of it ranked No. 1.

All Georgia had to do to hold onto the No. 1 spot was win at home against a nearly three-touchdown underdog. Instead, its loss to unranked Auburn meant the Bulldogs were No. 1 two days longer than Katie Zacharia was the White House press secretary.

That meant Notre Dame was in the prime spot to climb to the top. But the Irish failed their first true test of the season, losing 28-24 at BYU in a game that ended with two legitimate controversies that could have given Notre Dame a chance to win.

But it was Miami rising to the top spot with a referee-aided, double-overtime victory over Florida State , a reeling program that is holding yard sales to raise money to fire its coach.

If Miami did not escape, Ohio State would have returned to No. 1, unless, of course, Nick Marsh's left foot did not land partly out of bounds and Indiana held on to defeat the Buckeyes. Then it would have been the Hoosiers at the top.

All the while, BYU would have stated its case by beating what was then No. 2 Notre Dame.

All to point out, we do not know what we do not know about how this season ends.

Who would you take? Are you certain the national champion is going to come from the top 5 in the current poll? I am not.

Although I still believe the two best teams in the country are Ohio State and Georgia with the winner of the Nov. 7 Miami-Notre Dame emerging as a threat.

And do not discount a team or two outside the top 10 finding that spark — as Miami did the final month of the regular season a year ago — and making a run.

It all adds up to a wild, unpredictable second half of the college football season in which a prohibitive favorite may or may not emerge, but will ensure an entertaining playoff.

Tom D'Angelo is a senior sports columnist and reporter for The Palm Beach Post. He can be reached at tdangelo@pbpost.com.
